the source underwent a series of spectral and flux transitions between 1994 and 1995.
the transient black-hole X-ray source GRO J1744-28 underwent a series of gamma-ray spectral state transitions during 1994 September to 1995 October, when the source was in a low-intensity state.

the long-term variability of the transient gamma-ray source GRO J1744–24.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the spectral characteristics of GRO J1749-28 are consistent with the standard picture of black hole accretion disks.

the gamma-ray spectral state transitions in GRO J1716-24, as well as in GRO J04222+32 and Cyg X-1, are likely due to changes in the geometry of the accretion flow and/or the accreting matter's coupling to the central black hole, and that the gamma-ray emission is produced by the interaction of the accreted matter with the black hole.

the gamma-ray spectra are consistent with a model in which the high-intensity state is characterized by a thermal Comptonization component with a soft power-law component, while the low-intensity state is described by a soft power-law spectrum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gamma-ray spectral behavior of these systems is more complex than previously thought.

the gamma-ray spectral state transitions of GRO J 1719-24, as well as GRO J 0422+32, are consistent with a picture in which a hot and variable Comptonizing corona is responsible for the soft thermal emission, and in which the hard nonthermal emission originates in an optically thin, nonthermal electron component that is coupled to the Comptonizing corus, and that this nonthermal electron component is responsible for the spectral state transitions.

the soft gamma-ray spectral shape of the persistent emission from GRO J1716-24 is not as simple as a pure thermal Comptonization spectrum, but is a composite of a soft power law with a thermal Comptonization component.
